items.q: Why do unit tests matter more with agents?
items.a: Writing code is easy now—**verifying it is the bottleneck**, and tests give agents **CI feedback**.
**700+ merged PRs**, ~225K test lines, MVVM coverage **9% → 59%**.

items.q: How does the selector pick files?
items.a: It scores how **confidently an agent can test** each file—boosting view models, penalising legacy and big files.

items.q: How many actions does the lifecycle workflow take per PR?
items.a: **Exactly one** per pass: close, skip, fix, or assign a reviewer.

items.q: Who reviews an agent's test PR?
items.a: The **top git-blame contributor** of the file, with **auto-merge** on approval.

items.q: What happens when a reviewer rejects a PR?
items.a: The file goes into a **30-day cooldown**.

items.q: How did agents cheat to get green CI?
items.a: **Editing production code**, deleting or silencing tests, and adding long waits.
Close any PR that **touches a non-test file**.

items.q: What does the LLM judge catch?
items.a: Production edits, **weakened tests** and long waits—**73 of ~1,200** PRs rejected.
Running agents on **Mac runners** so they **build and lint locally** first.
